outcomes: A user who runs putnami init on a release channel gets a workspace whose extensions, template and starter dependencies all come from that channel
A release candidate is smoke-tested on its own immutable channel, whatever latest names and even while latest is empty
The workspace init creates pins no channel: its lock records exact versions, and putnami upgrade follows latest by default
nonGoals: Choosing an exact version: the release lines do not share one version, so one version cannot name a release set
Recording the install channel in a file: the name of the installed binary is the record, and putnami upgrade renames it
Resolving a release set through a provider: each registry resolves the channel natively
Changing putnami upgrade, putnami install or projects create run on its own

requirements.text: putnami init resolves on one channel: --channel, else PUTNAMI_CHANNEL, else the install record, else latest; stable reads latest. The install record is the tag of the name the running executable resolves to, putnami-<variant>-<tag>, unless it is a semantic version, a source build or dev. Any other name, such as the active putnami.exe on Windows, records nothing. An empty name, a name outside the portable channel alphabet and an exact version are usage errors raised before init writes or requests anything.

On a channel other than latest, every resolution of the run reads that channel and none reads latest: both extensions, the template, the template install project creation falls back to, the Go framework version (@v/<channel>.info where @latest is asked), and the workspace installers, which receive the putnami-channel job option. A channel that names no release fails the run instead of resolving latest. Init passes while latest names an older release set and while latest is empty.

Without a channel choice and without an install record, and on latest, init sends the requests it sent before it took a channel: bare artifact names, @latest for the Go framework, and no putnami-channel option.

The channel is a target of the init run only. putnami.workspace.json keeps bare artifact names, putnami.lock.json records the exact version, the digest and a version-pinned source of each artifact, and neither file names the channel. putnami upgrade reads neither PUTNAMI_CHANNEL nor the install record, and follows latest by default.

smoke-check-release.sh and smoke-check-release.ps1 export the channel they are started on as PUTNAMI_CHANNEL, after they clear every PUTNAMI_ variable and before the init leg, so the init command line stays the public one and a value the caller exported never reaches it.
